text:
maria: Heads up — after the 03:45 canary we started seeing 95th/99th latency spikes on short-context workloads. Root cause looks like kernel fallback when a few requests in the batch have much larger seqlen.
jon: Can you paste the kernel selection log?
maria: Sure. snippet below from runtime debug at 03:46 UTC:
```
[03:46:12] batch_id=457 kernel_pick=matmul_generic device=rtx-80 max_slen_in_batch=2048 median_slen=16 pick_reason=degraded_memory_estimate
[03:46:12] request=0 slen=16 path=prefill kernel=fast_fused_gemm
[03:46:12] request=1 slen=2048 path=decode kernel=matmul_generic fallback=true
[03:46:12] batch_latency_ms=142.3
```
maria: TL;DR: one long request in a batch pulls the whole batch into the generic kernel and thrashes KV cache, increasing latency for the short ones.
kevin: That's the pattern we've seen in production — the selector currently picks a single kernel per batch based on max_slen heuristic. When max_slen jumps, the autotuner doesn't guard with hysteresis.
sasha: @kevin can you check whether the autotune window had recent updates? Might be an aggressive learning rate.
kevin: Looks like autotuner applied new thresholds at 03:40 that lowered the long-context cutoff to 128 -> that would classify many mid-length requests as "long" and bias kernel picks.
anika: Two quick mitigation ideas: (1) enforce per-request kernel pinning for prefill vs decode paths so prefill short ctx stay on fast kernel, (2) split batches by seqlen tiers as a temporary patch.
jon: Splitting by seqlen tiers helps but increases scheduling overhead. Could we instead add a short-circuit: if median_slen < 64 and max_slen/mad_ratio > 8 then route long requests to a separate queue?
kevin: Agree, implementable: add MAD-based outlier detector in batcher and opportunistically peel out long ones before kernel selection. Low-risk and we keep batching benefits for majority.
perf-bot: perf-trace attached: https://perf.redwood/trace/457 (shows KV cache misses spike correlating with fallback) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maria: I've filed a quick PR with the outlier-peel change and a flag to opt-in per deployment. Will run canary tomorrow morning.
sasha: Also let's add an autotune safety: require 10 consecutive windows before reducing cutoff by >2x. Seems the aggressive change caused instability.
anika: Good call. Can we also add a metric that reports "kernel heterogeneity per batch" so ops can alert on mixed-path batches?
jon: Yes — new metric: batch_kernel_entropy and fraction_mispicked_by_slen. Set alert if >0.2 for 5m.
maria: I'll land the metrics + PR, and schedule an infra canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
kevin: After canary, let's run the profiler on the offending GPU model (rtx-80) with KV cache counters to confirm reduced thrash.
maria: Will update thread with canary results tomorrow.
